jobs.title: Graduate Planner
jobs.description:
**About the role**  

We are Balfour Beatty. You may not know us by name, but you’ll recognise what we do. We’re a leading international infrastructure group, building, maintaining and improving infrastructure that supports communities for generations to come.



As a Graduate Planner, you'll join our 2027 Early Careers programme and gain hands\-on experience while contributing to some of the UK's most significant infrastructure projects. From day one, you'll take on real responsibility, develop technical and professional skills, and work alongside experienced colleagues who will support your growth. You'll also be part of a supportive graduate community, building the skills, experience and industry\-recognised accreditations needed for a successful career.



In this role, you’ll join one of our Balfour Beatty Power T\&D teams as a Graduate Planner, based in Middlesbrough, supporting projects across UK.

 **What you'll be doing**  

As a Graduate Planner you’ll play an important role in supporting the planning and successful delivery of major infrastructure and construction projects. Working alongside experienced planners, engineers, and project teams, you'll apply your academic knowledge in a practical environment while developing the technical, analytical, and professional skills needed for a successful career in project planning and project controls.



You'll gain experience developing and maintaining project programmes, monitoring performance, analysing progress data, and supporting project teams to achieve delivery objectives. Through a structured graduate development programme, you'll build expertise in planning, project controls, programme management, forecasting, and project delivery while working towards professional accreditation..



You’ll support with:


* Supporting the day\-to\-day planning function across projects, helping to ensure programmes remain accurate, updated, and aligned with delivery requirements
* Developing, maintaining, and updating short\-term and long\-term project programmes to reflect progress and project changes
* Managing and updating project and contractual programmes in line with reporting requirements and project objectives
* Monitoring project progress, analysing programme performance, and identifying variances, risks, and opportunities
* Supporting the collection, analysis, and presentation of progress and performance information to support project decision\-making
* Applying planning techniques including sequencing, logic development, critical path analysis, resource planning, and forecasting
* Producing planning reports, programme updates, dashboards, and performance information for project teams and stakeholders
* Supporting project controls activities, including baseline management, change management, and programme assurance
* Working with project teams to understand project requirements, construction activities, and delivery strategies
* Supporting forecasting activities relating to labour, plant, materials, subcontractors, and project resources
* Building strong working relationships with project managers, engineers, subcontractors, and other stakeholders to support successful project delivery
* Contributing to continuous improvement initiatives that enhance programme management, reporting, and project performance
* Using industry\-standard planning software and digital tools to support project planning and controls activities

 **Who we're looking for**  

We value your potential over past experience and are looking for graduates with a degree in Construction Management/Construction Planning and a genuine interest in our industry. To be eligible, you’ll need to achieve a minimum 2:2 honours degree by the time you start.



We’d love to receive your application if you:


* Are curious, proactive and motivated to develop professionally.
* Enjoy solving problems and finding practical solutions.
* Work well with others and build positive relationships.
* Communicate clearly and confidently with different people.
* Take ownership, adapt to challenges and are committed to achieving results.



Please note that this role may require travel to various locations, which means you may occasionally need to work and stay away from home. Flexibility is essential, as assignments can vary based on project needs. All reasonable travel and accommodation expenses will be reimbursed in accordance with company policy. Before joining Balfour Beatty, you must hold a full UK driver's license.

 **Why work for us as a Graduate*** Work on high\-profile projects that make a real difference, while building your career with one of the UK’s leading infrastructure groups.
* Be part of a supportive early careers network, with structured training and with structured training and coaching from experienced industry professionals.
* Take part in unique development experiences, including residential trips in the Lake District and personal development delivered by our external partners.
* Take ownership of your ongoing professional development, with support towards professional membership and chartership or professional registration where relevant to your career path.


**What we can offer you**


* Competitive salary and flexible benefits, giving you the freedom to shape a rewards package that works for you.
* 25 days' holiday, with the option to buy or sell additional days.
* A permanent contract from day one, reflecting our commitment to your long\-term career.
* Clear progression opportunities, with bi\-annual performance and pay reviews throughout your programme.
* Opportunities to connect with fellow graduates through networking events, development activities and our Early Careers Showcase.
* Opportunities to get involved in wider business initiatives, community projects and programmes such as the Duke of Edinburgh's Award.

 **About us**  

The power sector is one of the fastest\-growing areas in infrastructure, helping to keep homes, businesses and communities connect

jobs.title: Junior Town Planner
jobs.description:
**Junior Town Planner**

Location: Doncaster — office based at our sister company

Salary: £27,000–£30,000 per annum, depending on experience

NAPC is an innovative and growing planning consultancy specialising in annexes, garden rooms, mobile homes and residential development. We’re looking for a motivated Junior Town Planner to join our team, develop their planning knowledge and gain practical experience across a varied range of projects.

**About the role**

You’ll be based at our sister company’s office in Doncaster, working alongside their team while receiving planning supervision and mentoring remotely from NAPC’s planning team.

You’ll be the only planner based in the Doncaster office, so this role would suit someone who is comfortable working independently, communicates proactively and knows when to ask for guidance. Your local colleagues will provide day\-to\-day workplace support, while NAPC will provide the technical planning advice, feedback and support you need to develop.

We welcome applications from graduates and early\-career planners. Your responsibilities will grow with your experience and confidence, with guidance and review from senior colleagues.

**Key responsibilities**

* Assist with preparing and progressing planning applications and appeals.
* Research planning policies, site histories and development constraints.
* Help prepare site appraisals, planning statements and feasibility assessments.
* Support senior planners with client accounts and project coordination.
* Liaise with clients, local authorities and other professionals, with guidance from the NAPC team.
* Keep accurate project records and contribute ideas to improve our systems and workflows.

**What we’re looking for**

* A degree in Town Planning or a related discipline.
* An interest in UK planning and development management.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills and attention to detail.
* Good organisational skills and the ability to manage tasks and priorities.
* A proactive approach to learning, seeking feedback and keeping colleagues updated.
* The confidence to work independently within a wider team, with support provided remotely.

**What we offer**

* A salary of £27,000–£30,000 per annum, depending on experience.
* Flexible working hours by agreement.
* Remote mentoring, technical guidance and project review from NAPC’s planning team.
* A welcoming office environment within our sister company in Doncaster.
* Practical experience across a variety of planning applications, appeals and development projects.
* Opportunities to take on greater responsibility as your skills develop.

**Interested in joining us?**

Submit your CV via Indeed or email info@napc.uk. We’d welcome a short covering note explaining your interest in the role and any relevant experience from your studies or employment.

Ability to commute/relocate: You must be able to reliably commute to our Doncaster office or relocate before starting work.

Work location: In person, Doncaster.

NEW00027W Requisition \#  

Graduate Town Planning Consultant\- Newcastle


See it differently \- Early Careers at Arup


See it differently


You see the world through a unique lens and that’s exactly what we need. We embrace how you see things differently – it’s essential for creating a sustainable future.


Arup is a global consultancy with advisory and technical expertise across more than 150 disciplines. We guide, plan and design the future of the built environment. Globally, each year we recruit hundreds of graduates and students who help us see things differently and solve the most complex challenges facing our clients, climate and communities.


The Opportunity


We have a small growing town planning team based in Newcastle that works on local and national projects across Development Management, Policy and Infrastructure workstreams. Our projects are a mixture of those which we lead multidisciplinary teams or single discipline commissions as well as those where we provide technical expertise on projects led by others, including external collaborators. We sit within a national network of over 100 town planners based around all our UK offices as well as within the Cities, Planning and Design portfolio, which includes transport planning and economic development. As we work across all internal Arup portfolios, we have a great variety in our work as well as with a range of external clients across sectors, we have great variety in our day\-to\-day work, collaborating with a wide range of external clients across sectors.


* Undertake planning policy review and analysis
* Review site constraints and opportunities
* Draft reports, briefing notes and consultation responses
* Work collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams
* Prepare planning applications and supporting statements

Is this role right for you?


For this opportunity, we are seeking the following qualifications, skills and attributes:


An undergraduate or bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in a relevant discipline, such as Urban Planning, Geography, Urban Design or a related planning subject.


Required for this role, Understanding of the UK planning system (TCPA, DCO, Local Plans, NPPF); strong report writing; critical thinker/ problem solver; policy interpretation; research and evidence assessment; stakeholder engagement; presentation skills; consultation analysis; consultation monitoring and responses; time management and managing multiple workstreams; team collaboration; familiar with key software packages (e.g. strong skills in MS Excel, Word, PowerPoint, SharePoint, MS Teams, Copilot, etc)


Desirable skills the above but with greater depth/ competency plus basic to intermediate GIS skills; appreciation of development viability, programme and risk considerations and client\-focussed thinking; interest in regeneration, policy, and infrastructure


To be considered for a graduate opportunity, your application must include a copy of your academic transcript and meet the following criteria:

Alongside your degree, we look for the following core attributes;


* Changemakers: A passion for sustainable development and creating a better world is key.
* Innovative minds: We’re looking for critical thinkers who embrace new ideas and challenge the status quo.
* Growth seekers: You have a growth mindset, always eager to learn and explore new ways of working.
* Adaptable adventurers: You’re ready to take on any challenge that comes your way.

Please note, in the event of high applicant volume, this role may be closed ahead of the advertised closing date. Early application is recommended.


Eligibility


Please note that we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role. Therefore, you must ensure that you are eligible to work permanently in the UK without our sponsorship.

In addition, you’ll have access to flexible benefits to help you look after all aspects of your wellbeing and give you the freedom and flexibility to find the best solutions for you, your family, and your individual needs.


Next Steps


We've designed our application process to be straightforward and supportive, giving you the opportunity to showcase your skills and potential. Applications are reviewed as they're received, so we encourage you to apply as early as possible.

jobs.title: Land & Planning Analyst
jobs.description:
Land \& Planning Analyst

Location: Hemel Hempstead, Hertfordshire  
Salary: £30,000–£35,000 \+ performance\-related bonus, depending on experience  
Reports to: Head of Investment  
Role: Full\-time

About the role

The Life Less Ordinary Group (LLO) is looking for an ambitious Land \& Planning Analyst to join our investment and development team in Hemel Hempstead.

This is a commercially focused role combining planning, land acquisition and development appraisal, suited to someone who has already gained practical professional experience within planning, land or residential development and is looking to move into a more commercial, developer\-side role.

You will have at least 12 months' relevant professional experience, and may currently be working as a Graduate or Assistant Planner within a planning consultancy or local planning authority, or in an early\-career land, development or acquisition role with a developer, housebuilder, land promoter or land agency.

The primary objective of the role is clear: to proactively identify residential development opportunities that LLO can acquire, option or secure subject to planning.

You will work alongside our existing network of land agents, planning consultants and professional advisers, while building a direct pipeline of on\- and off\-market opportunities.

This is not a traditional planning role.

We are looking for someone who understands the planning system but wants to use that knowledge commercially — identifying where planning policy, site history, ownership, constraints or changing circumstances could create an opportunity to unlock development value.

A significant part of the role will involve proactively searching for opportunities rather than simply assessing sites already being marketed. This means investigating planning histories, Local Plans, land ownership, site allocations, refusals, appeals and policy changes to identify land with development potential that others may have overlooked.

You will work directly with the Head of Investment on live opportunities, initially focusing on site sourcing, planning research, site screening and first\-stage development appraisal.

As your experience and commercial judgement develop, you will gain increasing responsibility for landowner and agent relationships, planning strategy, development appraisal, heads of terms, option agreements, conditional contracts, subject\-to\-planning transactions and land negotiations.

For the right person, this role provides a clear route towards becoming a Land Buyer.

Key responsibilities

You will:

* Proactively identify on\- and off\-market residential development opportunities across LLO's target areas using Searchland and other land, ownership and planning intelligence platforms.
* Source opportunities across a range of site types and scales, including small infill and sub\-10\-unit schemes, brownfield and redevelopment sites, grey belt and Green Belt opportunities, allocated and emerging allocation sites, and larger strategic land opportunities.
* Look beyond land actively being marketed, using planning policy, ownership information, site history, development constraints and changing circumstances to identify sites where development potential may not yet have been recognised by the market.
* Research land ownership, planning history, surrounding land uses and development constraints to identify sites with unrealised development potential.
* Monitor emerging planning policy and circumstances that could create acquisition opportunities, including Local Plan reviews, call\-for\-sites exercises, housing land supply positions, site allocations, planning applications, refusals, appeal decisions and changes to national planning policy.
* Review relevant planning applications and appeal decisions to understand how planning policy is being interpreted and identify opportunities relevant to LLO's acquisition strategy.
* Undertake initial site assessments covering planning potential, key constraints, indicative development capacity and likely planning strategy.
* Prepare first\-pass development appraisals considering indicative GDV, development costs, land value and development margin, with support and review from the Head of Investment.
* Prepare concise site opportunity reports setting out the opportunity, planning position, principal risks, indicative development potential and recommendation on whether the site warrants further investigation.
* Build relationships with landowners, land agents, planning consultants and other property professionals to generate direct and off\-market opportunities.
* Undertake direct approaches to landowners where appropriate and proactively follow up potential opportunities.
* Maintain an accurate and live land pipeline, recording opportunities, approaches, appraisals, current status and next actions.
* Attend site visits and meetings with landowners, agents, planning consultants and other professional advisers.
* Support the Head of Investment in progressing opportunities through heads of terms, option agreements, conditional contracts and subject\-to\-planning transactions.
* Progressively take greater responsibility for originating opportunities, landowner relationships, site recommendations, deal structuring and negotiation as your experience develops.

The Head of Investment will initially retain responsibility for final appraisal, deal structure, negotiation strategy and acquisition sign\-off, while supporting your progression towards taking greater ownership of these areas.

* Degree in Town Planning, Urban Planning, Real Estate, Land Economy, Geography or another relevant built\-environment discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.
* At least 12 months' relevant professional experience within a planning consultancy, local planning authority, residential developer, housebuilder, land promoter, land agency or other relevant property environment.
* A practical understanding of th

jobs.title: Planning Consultant
jobs.description:
**Overview**

Calling all planners!

We're Growing... Come and Join Us.

Wignalls Chartered Surveyors is continuing to grow, and we're looking to expand our planning team with either an experienced Chartered Planner or an experienced Planning Consultant!

Planning has become one of the fastest growing parts of our business, and we're looking for people who enjoy solving problems, working with clients and delivering successful outcomes.

What makes our team different is the way we work together. Every application is discussed, challenged and refined as a team. We constantly bounce ideas off one another, drawing on each other's experience to make sure every submission is as robust as it can possibly be. That collaborative approach, combined with a genuine team spirit, is something we're incredibly proud of and is a key reason why we achieve such a high success rate.

Whether you're preparing planning applications, advising clients, negotiating with local planning authorities or helping to shape development proposals, you'll be surrounded by people who genuinely want to help each other succeed.

We're looking for someone who has strong planning knowledge, excellent communication skills and enjoys building relationships with clients. If you're an experienced planner, you'll have the opportunity to take ownership of your own projects while working alongside an experienced multidisciplinary team. If you're a graduate, we'll provide the support, mentoring and experience needed to help you develop your career.

In return, we offer a highly competitive salary, excellent career progression, a company car if required, private healthcare if required, ongoing professional development and the opportunity to be part of a business that is growing quickly and investing in its people.

We're not looking for someone who simply wants another planning job. We're looking for someone who wants to be part of building one of the leading planning teams in the North West.

If that sounds like you, we'd love to hear from you. Please send your CV in confidence or get in touch for an informal chat.

Pay: £25,420\.00\-£50,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* Company events
* Free parking
* On\-site parking
* Private medical insurance
* Work from home

Work Location: In person

Our culture is deeply ingrained in our core values of Integrity, Trust, Respect, Unity, Service, and Teamwork (ITRUST). **Department**: Planning **Salary**: Commensurate with Experience/Education
**Description**:


The Geographic Information Systems (GIS) Analyst supports campus planning, operations, research, and public engagement by building, maintaining, and analyzing geospatial datasets and creating high\-quality maps, dashboards, and web apps.


1\. Collects, cleans, and maintains geospatial datasets (parcels, buildings, utilities, land use, mobility, environmental layers) using ESRI ArcGIS Pro/Enterprise/Online and related tools.


2\. Produces cartographically sound maps, web maps, and StoryMaps for planning studies, capital projects, emergency response, and campus wayfinding.


3\. Builds and manages campus basemaps, feature services, and symbology libraries; ensures consistent standards across projects.


4\. Performs spatial analyses (network, proximity, suitability, density, overlay, 3D scene/visibility) and summarizes results in clear tables, graphics, and dashboards.


5\. Develops repeatable workflows for recurring analyses (e.g., space utilization, mobility and access, sustainability metrics, environmental risk).


6\. Integrates CAD/BIM, survey, and remote\-sensing (e.g., LiDAR, aerial imagery) into GIS; reconciles coordinate systems and dimensional accuracy.


7\. Establishes metadata, versioning, QA/QC checks, and data governance aligned with university standards.


8\. Documents processes and maintains a data catalog for campus stakeholders.


9\. Configures ArcGIS dashboards, web apps, and features editing experiences for non\-technical users.


10\. Uses Python/ArcPy, ModelBuilder, and/or FME to automate ETL, data validation, and map production.


11\. Supports geospatial components of regulatory reporting (e.g., environmental, ADA accessibility, safety zones) and data privacy requirements.


12\. Maintains continuity plans for GIS services and contributes to emergency mapping when needed.


13\. Performs other job\-related as assigned.


**Department is willing to accept education in lieu of experience.**


MQ: Education: Requires a thorough understanding of both theoretical and practical aspects of an analytical, technical or professional discipline; or the basic knowledge of more than one professional discipline. Knowledge of the discipline is normally obtained through a formal, directly job\-related 4\-year degree from a college or university or an equivalent in\-depth specialized training program that is directly related to the type of work being performed.


Preferred: Degree in Geography/Geospatial Science, Urban Planning, Environmental Science, GIS, Computer Science, or related field or associate's degree with 25 years of professional GIS experience (higher\-education or public sector preferred).


Experience: Requires a minimum of three (3\) years of directly job\-related experience. Preferred: Experience integrating CAD/BIM, survey, and remote sensing into campus GIS. 3D GIS (Scene Viewer, ArcGIS Urban), network analysis, and mobility/accessibility modeling. Familiarity with open\-source tools (QGIS), cloud GIS, and versioned enterprise geodatabases. Prior work supporting campus planning, facilities management, sustainability programs, or emergency operations.


Certification/Licensing: None.


All positions at the University of Houston\-System are security sensitive and will require a criminal history check.


The University of Houston System and its universities are Equal Opportunity Institutions. Everyone is encouraged to apply.

jobs.title: Planner / GIS Analyst
jobs.description:
**Job Summary**
---------------



E\-Logic, Inc. is seeking a **Planner / GIS Analyst** to support the development of a **25\-Year Real Property Master Plan** for the Virgin Islands National Guard.



The Planner / GIS Analyst will develop and organize the project's GIS database, compile and analyze spatial information, map existing conditions and planning constraints, and produce professional maps, graphics, and other visual materials supporting the master planning effort.



The selected candidate will work closely with the Senior Master Planner and multidisciplinary project team to support site assessments, land\-use analysis, environmental constraint mapping, facility planning, and preparation of the final master plan.


**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------


### **GIS Database Development**


* Build and organize an installation **GIS database** from available source information.
* Compile, clean, organize, and manage spatial and non\-spatial data.
* Develop GIS layers for facilities, land use, infrastructure, transportation, environmental constraints, and other relevant planning factors.
* Maintain data quality, accuracy, organization, and metadata.

### **GIS Analysis \& Mapping**


* Map land\-use opportunities and constraints supporting long\-range installation planning.
* Conduct spatial analysis to support land\-use and development recommendations.
* Analyze existing conditions and spatial relationships among facilities, infrastructure, environmental resources, and development areas.
* Integrate GIS information with planning, facility, environmental, and infrastructure data.

### **Planning Support**


* Support installation site assessments and field data collection.
* Assist the Senior Master Planner with planning analyses and development recommendations.
* Support preparation of Area Development Plans and other planning exhibits.
* Provide GIS analysis and mapping support for master planning activities.

### **Maps \& Graphics**


* Produce professional maps, exhibits, graphics, and figures for master plan deliverables.

* Verify spatial data and map products for accuracy and consistency.
* Assist with preparation of supporting technical documentation and planning materials.

**Qualifications**

* Minimum **5 years of professional experience** in GIS, planning, or a related discipline.

* Experience mapping **land\-use and environmental constraints**.
* Experience producing maps and graphics for planning, engineering, environmental, or similar technical documents.
* Proficiency with **ArcGIS Pro**.
* Working knowledge of **AutoCAD**.
* Proficiency with **Microsoft Office**.
* Strong analytical and organizational skills.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills.
* Ability to work independently in a primarily remote environment.

**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------


* Experience with **DoD GIS data standards**.
* Experience supporting military installations, National Guard facilities, federal facilities, or military bases.

* Environmental planning or environmental constraints analysis experience.
* Experience integrating GIS with land\-use, facility, infrastructure, or real property planning.
* Federal or DoD project experience.
* Experience in the **U.S. Virgin Islands, Caribbean, or similar island environments**.

**Work Environment \& Travel**

This position is **primarily remote and part\-time**. The selected candidate must be comfortable working independently and coordinating remotely with the Senior Master Planner and project team.



Approximately **one trip to St. Croix and/or St. Thomas, U.S. Virgin Islands**, is anticipated during the one\-year period of performance.

**Department**: Planning **Salary**: Commensurate with Experience/Education
**Description**:


The Geographic Information Systems (GIS) Analyst supports campus planning, operations, research, and public engagement by building, maintaining, and analyzing geospatial datasets and creating high\-quality maps, dashboards, and web apps.


1\. Collects, cleans, and maintains geospatial datasets (parcels, buildings, utilities, land use, mobility, environmental layers) using ESRI ArcGIS Pro/Enterprise/Online and related tools.


2\. Produces cartographically sound maps, web maps, and StoryMaps for planning studies, capital projects, emergency response, and campus wayfinding.


3\. Builds and manages campus basemaps, feature services, and symbology libraries; ensures consistent standards across projects.


4\. Performs spatial analyses (network, proximity, suitability, density, overlay, 3D scene/visibility) and summarizes results in clear tables, graphics, and dashboards.


5\. Develops repeatable workflows for recurring analyses (e.g., space utilization, mobility and access, sustainability metrics, environmental risk).


6\. Integrates CAD/BIM, survey, and remote\-sensing (e.g., LiDAR, aerial imagery) into GIS; reconciles coordinate systems and dimensional accuracy.


7\. Establishes metadata, versioning, QA/QC checks, and data governance aligned with university standards.


8\. Documents processes and maintains a data catalog for campus stakeholders.


9\. Configures ArcGIS dashboards, web apps, and features editing experiences for non\-technical users.


10\. Uses Python/ArcPy, ModelBuilder, and/or FME to automate ETL, data validation, and map production.


11\. Supports geospatial components of regulatory reporting (e.g., environmental, ADA accessibility, safety zones) and data privacy requirements.


12\. Maintains continuity plans for GIS services and contributes to emergency mapping when needed.


13\. Performs other job\-related as assigned.


**Department is willing to accept education in lieu of experience.**


MQ: Education: Requires a thorough understanding of both theoretical and practical aspects of an analytical, technical or professional discipline; or the basic knowledge of more than one professional discipline. Knowledge of the discipline is normally obtained through a formal, directly job\-related 4\-year degree from a college or university or an equivalent in\-depth specialized training program that is directly related to the type of work being performed.


Preferred: Degree in Geography/Geospatial Science, Urban Planning, Environmental Science, GIS, Computer Science, or related field or associate's degree with 25 years of professional GIS experience (higher\-education or public sector preferred).


Experience: Requires a minimum of three (3\) years of directly job\-related experience. Preferred: Experience integrating CAD/BIM, survey, and remote sensing into campus GIS. 3D GIS (Scene Viewer, ArcGIS Urban), network analysis, and mobility/accessibility modeling. Familiarity with open\-source tools (QGIS), cloud GIS, and versioned enterprise geodatabases. Prior work supporting campus planning, facilities management, sustainability programs, or emergency operations.


Certification/Licensing: None.


All positions at the University of Houston\-System are security sensitive and will require a criminal history check.
